causal-factors.name: Historical 100m+ auction precedent
causal-factors.rationale: Past public auctions at Christie’s and Sotheby’s have exceeded US$100 million multiple times (e.g., 2010 Picasso, 2012 The Scream, 2015 Picasso, 2017 Salvator Mundi, 2025 Klimt), establishing a nontrivial baseline likelihood for another such sale.

causal-factors.name: Market momentum from record prices and rising top-tier valuations
causal-factors.rationale: Continued record sales and price inflation for the world’s most prestigious works amplify bidding enthusiasm and the probability of reaching or surpassing the 100m threshold.

causal-factors.name: Ultra-high-net-worth buyer demand and cross-border participation
causal-factors.rationale: Growing appetite from global ultra-wealthy collectors (including regions like Asia and the Middle East) increases competitive bidding for marquee lots.

causal-factors.name: Provenance/attribution clarity and work prestige
causal-factors.rationale: Clear attribution and strong provenance elevate bidder confidence and can unlock premium pricing at auction.

causal-factors.name: Macroeconomic headwinds and market volatility
causal-factors.rationale: Economic uncertainty or liquidity constraints can dampen willingness to bid at ultra-high price points in any given window.

causal-factors.name: Supply constraints and rarity of comparable works entering the market
causal-factors.rationale: A limited pipeline of comparable masterpieces increases competition when such works are offered, raising the odds of crossing the 100m threshold.

causal-factors.name: Historical precedent for 100m+ public art sales at Christie’s/Sotheby’s
causal-factors.rationale: Past public sales have broken the 100m mark multiple times (Picasso Nude, Green Leaves and Bust in 2010; Munch The Scream in 2012; Picasso Les Femmes d’Algers Version O in 2015; Salvator Mundi in 2017; Klimt Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer in 2025), showing such an outcome is plausible.

causal-factors.name: Klimt 2025 record sale at Sotheby’s
causal-factors.rationale: Klimt’s Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer sold for $236.4m in 2025 at Sotheby’s, illustrating that a painting can exceed $100m in a single public auction and broaden the tail risk.

causal-factors.name: Phillips' historical capacity for 100m+ single-lot sales
causal-factors.rationale: Phillips has rarely achieved a $100m+ single-lot sale; its 2018 London auction performed strongly in total but did not feature a confirmed $100m+ single-lot sale, making a Phillips-led $100m+ auction less likely.

causal-factors.name: High-end market headwinds in 2024-2025
causal-factors.rationale: The Art Basel/UBS Global Art Market Report 2025 shows a 12% decline in 2024 with the high end thinning, signaling risks to another $100m+ public auction in the near term.

causal-factors.name: Ultra-wealthy buyers and cross-border demand
causal-factors.rationale: Historic ultra-wealthy buyers (e.g., the Saudi prince identified as Salvator Mundi’s buyer) and large private collections show continued top-end demand that could support a $100m+ public sale.

causal-factors.name: US market liquidity and share of art sales
causal-factors.rationale: The US accounted for about 43% of global art sales in 2024, indicating strong liquidity that could enable a $100m+ auction.

causal-factors.name: Klimt Portrait of Elisabeth Lederer (Sotheby’s, NY, Nov 2025)
causal-factors.rationale: A $236.4M sale demonstrates the top end of the market can exceed $100M, lifting near-term odds of a public $100M+ painting sale before May 1, 2026.

causal-factors.name: Leonardo da Vinci Salvator Mundi (Christie’s, NY, 2017)
causal-factors.rationale: A $450.3M public auction record shows the $100M+ threshold is routinely attainable under current market conditions.

causal-factors.name: Historical $100M+ public paintings records (e.g., Picasso 2015, Scream 2012, Bacon 2013)
causal-factors.rationale: Multiple past public auctions above $100M indicate the event is achievable within major houses’ cycles.

causal-factors.name: Top-end art-market slowdown in 2023-2024 (Art Basel/UBS, The Art Newspaper)
causal-factors.rationale: Macro headwinds and cooling demand at the high end could dampen near-term probability of new $100M+ records.

causal-factors.name: Rising new-buyer share in high-end art (UBS 2025)
causal-factors.rationale: An influx of new buyers (e.g., 44% new to dealers, 38% first-time buyers) could fuel trophy purchases and raise odds of a $100M+ sale.

synthesis: The baseline ensemble sits at 53%, but near-term macro headwinds, Phillips' limited track record at or above $100m, and the very tight two-month horizon justify a modest downward adjustment. Historical outliers still show such sales are possible, so a probability around 50% with a ±8% range captures the balanced view.
